extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting manuscripts to Nature Communications (corresponding authors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines describing Nature Communications' submission, editorial assessment, peer review, revision, acceptance, transparent review, reviewer acknowledgement, appeals, and preprint policies for original research submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and required declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscripts should be submitted via the online submission system. The corresponding author should indicate whether the work has been discussed with a specific Nature Communications editor before submission. Copies of any papers containing related work that are under consideration or in-press at other journals should be included with the submission as additional supplementary information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal's online system; declare prior discussions with editors; include related manuscripts under consideration elsewhere as supplementary information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary editor evaluates the novelty and potential impact of the work, the appropriateness for the journal's editorial scope, the conceptual or methodological advances described in the paper, and its potential interest to Nature Communications' readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions that meet these editorial criteria are sent out to external referees; initial editorial assessment determines if the manuscript proceeds to peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty assessment specifics
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty is considered compromised if the submission has significant conceptual overlap with a published paper or one accepted for publication by Nature Communications. Preprint archives do not compromise novelty. Papers published independently while the manuscript is under review or revision at Nature Communications are not considered to compromise novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume preprints affect novelty; conceptual overlap with work already published or accepted at this journal is problematic; independent publication elsewhere during review does not automatically compromise novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript transfer from other Nature journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper was previously reviewed at another Nature journal, authors can use an automated manuscript transfer service to transfer referees' reports to Nature Communications. Editors will take previous reviews into account, though they may seek additional referees. Authors may instead request a fresh review, but this decision must be made at initial submission and cannot be changed later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If asking editors to consider previous reviews, include a note explaining the relationship between submissions and a point-by-point response to referees; in some high-quality cases papers can be accepted without further review, but serious prior criticisms will be considered; the received date will be the date of submission to Nature Communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review initiation and reviewer exclusion/suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author is notified when the editor decides to send a paper for review. At submission, authors may indicate a limited number of named scientists who should not review the paper. Authors may also suggest referees, though suggestions are not always followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excluded scientists must be identified by name; suggesting referees can be helpful but is not binding on editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee anonymity and signed reports
rubrics_metrics.description: By policy, referees are not identified to the authors, except when they sign their reports to the authors. Nature Communications supports reviewers signing their reports to authors if they wish. Referee reports, whether signed or not, are subsequently shared with the other reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may opt to sign reports; if they sign, their name may be associated with their report in the peer review file or with acknowledgement if they consent to being named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint policy and 'In Review' service
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Research encourages preprint deposition of originally submitted manuscripts. Authors may opt into 'In Review', a free preprint posting service integrated with submission; the preprint will be posted when editors decide whether to send the manuscript for external review and will be displayed as 'under review at Nature Research' if the manuscript is sent to reviewers. Authors may also deposit on any community-recognised preprint server at their discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting via 'In Review' happens at a specific editorial decision point; authors retain choice over preprint posting and server selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparent peer review policy and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Communications publishes reviewer comments to the authors and author rebuttal letters of revised versions of published research articles under a transparent peer review system. For manuscripts submitted before 1 November 2022 authors could opt out; submissions received on or after 1 November 2022 will have reviewer comments and rebuttals published alongside accepted original research articles. Transferred manuscripts will not have reviewer reports or rebuttals published for versions considered at the originating Nature journal. The peer review file is published as a supplementary file but does not contain editorial discussions, editorial decision letters, or any confidential comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scheme applies only to original research articles, not Review articles or other content; peer review files are supplementary and omit confidential editorial material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of the published peer review file
rubrics_metrics.description: The published peer review file will not contain all information considered in editorial decision making, such as discussions between editors, editorial decision letters, or any confidential comments made by reviewers or authors to the editors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should not consider the peer review file as a complete record of all editorial deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer acknowledgement and naming policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Communications formally acknowledges reviewers' contributions. All peer-reviewed content will carry an anonymous statement of peer reviewer acknowledgement, and for reviewers who give consent the journal will publish their names alongside the published article. If reviewers opt in to being named, names appear in alphabetical order; anonymous reviewers are acknowledged using a modified statement; if no reviewers agree to be named, a generic acknowledgement to anonymous reviewers is used. Names are not linked to specific reports unless the reviewer chose to sign their comments to the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer naming requires reviewer consent; conventions for ordering and anonymity are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision after review — editors weigh present quality and potential after revision
rubrics_metrics.description: When deciding after review, editors consider not only how good the paper is now but also how good it might become after revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions can be based on anticipated improvements after revision, not solely the current version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision requests for well-defined changes
rubrics_metrics.description: If referees have requested well-defined changes that do not appear to require extensive further experiments, editors may request a revised manuscript addressing the referees' concerns. The revised version is normally sent back to some or all of the original referees for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision letters will specify a deadline (typically two months); revisions returned within this period retain their original submission date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection with option to resubmit and submission-date policy
rubrics_metrics.description: If referees' concerns are more wide-ranging, editors will normally reject the manuscript; however, if the work has potential interest the editors may express interest in seeing a future resubmission. Resubmitted manuscripts may be sent to original or new referees at editors' discretion. Revised manuscripts resubmitted after such a rejection will not retain their earlier submission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should note that resubmissions after rejection do not keep prior submission dates and may be re-reviewed anew.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission documentation and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised manuscript should be accompanied by a cover letter explaining changes and a separate point-by-point response to referees' comments. A maximum of two resubmissions will be considered for each manuscript, after which a final decision on publication will be made. An invited revision must be submitted via the revision link to the online submission system, not as a new manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the required documentation format; respect the two-resubmission limit; use the revision link provided in decision letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final submission requirements and format compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for final submission is sent when the paper is nearly ready to publish, possibly requiring text changes but no revisions to data or conclusions. The final submission must comply with the journal's format requirements summarized in the Nature Communications manuscript checklist. For the final revision, authors should use the revision link to upload a final version of the text and high-resolution electronic files of final figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure compliance with the manuscript checklist and submit high-resolution figures; final submissions correspond to minor editorial changes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy-editing, proofs, and editorial control over style
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance, a copy editor may make changes so the manuscript is readable and clear to those outside the field and so that papers conform to the journal's style. Contributors are sent proofs and may discuss proposed changes, but Nature Communications reserves the right to make the final decision about matters of style and the size of figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors can discuss proofs but final editorial decisions about style/figure sizing rest with the journal; expect copyediting for clarity and broader readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article in Press policy and post-acceptance status
rubrics_metrics.description: Once formally accepted the article is published immediately as an Article in Press (an early access version of an accepted manuscript), allowing earlier access; it may be subject to further editing and is not yet the Version of Record. The Article in Press will be watermarked and carry legal disclaimers. Corrections and amendments will not be made to the Article in Press as the accepted manuscript still goes through proofing where such items can be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should use proofs to correct remaining issues; the Article in Press is not final and may be edited before Version of Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and complaints policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may ask editors to reconsider a negative decision (an appeal), but appeals are processed with lower priority than new submissions. Decisions can be reversed on appeal only if authors provide convincing evidence that the original decision was based on a factual error or biased reviewer comments. If an appeal merits further consideration, editors may send the authors' response or the revised paper to referees or ask an additional referee to comment; editors may also obtain advice from an additional referee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals require strong, convincing evidence; complaints about publication ethics or processes follow a separate policy and link.
